title: Add 5 pairs to your quotes list
summary: Use the Quotes tab to add 3 majors, 1 minor and 1 exotic [[currency-pair]], and note each one's [[spread]].

steps.text: Open MetaTrader and go to the Quotes tab.
Tap the button to add a symbol, usually shown as a plus sign at the top of the Quotes tab.
Search for or browse to a major pair such as EUR/USD, then tap it to add it. Some brokers add extra letters to symbol names, for example a suffix after EURUSD.
Add two more majors, such as USD/JPY and GBP/USD.
Add one minor (cross) pair, such as EUR/GBP.
Add one exotic pair, such as USD/ZAR, if your broker offers it.
Go back to the Quotes tab and check all 5 pairs are listed.
For each pair, write down the bid and ask and work out the spread in pips.

afterQuestions.prompt: Of the pairs you added, which type usually shows the widest spread?

options.explanation: Right: exotics usually trade less, so their spreads tend to be wider.
No: EUR/USD is among the most traded pairs and usually has one of the tightest spreads.

afterQuestions.prompt: You search for EURUSD and see a name like EURUSD with extra letters on the end. What does that most likely mean?

options.text: It is a different currency pair
options.explanation: No: it is still euro against US dollar. Check the symbol's details if unsure.

options.text: Your broker names its symbols with a suffix
options.explanation: Right: brokers can add letters to symbol names, often for different account types.
